articles.title: Thousands of dead fish found along Yamuna banks in Delhi’s Burari - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
NEW DELHI: Hundreds, possibly thousands, of dead fish were found along the banks of the Yamuna near Burari in north Delhi, raising fresh concerns over the river's water quality and the health of its aquatic ecosystem, the New Delhi Nature Society said on Thursday.
The society, which describes itself as a "A collective of individuals. Spreading awareness..." on its X profile, shared photographs and videos on Wednesday evening showing dead fish along the riverbank.
"Specific cause not established. Locals allege chemical waste discharged from Haryana through canals. Could it be related to the acid rain on Oct 12th?" it said in a post on X.
According to the society, fish deaths can indicate ecological stress, including deteriorating water quality, low levels of dissolved oxygen and the presence of toxic substances.
The cause of the latest fish deaths remains unclear.
The visuals have emerged amid continued concerns over pollution in the Yamuna, which continues to face pollution-related challenges despite repeated efforts to clean the river.
Mass fish deaths were also reported from Burari in May last year. At the time, visuals showed thousands of dead fish floating in the river, with locals attributing the deaths to chemical waste allegedly discharged from Haryana.
Reports had also pointed to high pollution levels.
In May this year, hundreds of fish died at Sanjay Lake in east Delhi amid a heatwave and falling water levels. Experts had cited a combination of high temperatures, concentrated pollutants and declining dissolved oxygen levels as possible factors.
(With inputs from PTI)

articles.title: SC seeks Centre’s reply on Jantar Mantar protest-site ban - Newsband
articles.full_text:
SC seeks Centre’s reply on Jantar Mantar protest-site ban
New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Thursday, October 15, sought the Centre’s response to a petition challenging the de-notification of Jantar Mantar as Delhi’s designated protest site, questioning whether an October 9 court observation had been used to justify the decision.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi issued notice on a plea filed by advocate Swaty Singh. The petition argues that removing Jantar Mantar as a protest venue infringes citizens’ fundamental rights to freedom of speech and expression and peaceful assembly.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, told the court that the October 9 order was not the basis for the decision. He said a committee had been constituted to examine alternative venues and had submitted a detailed report.
The petitioner argued that protesters must have a meaningful platform to communicate their grievances to the authorities. She said restrictions should not render the right to peaceful assembly ineffective.
The development follows a Delhi Police standing order issued by Commissioner Anurag Kumar on October 11. It de-notified Jantar Mantar and designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi as alternative venues for demonstrations.
On October 9, the Supreme Court had asked authorities to reconsider the decades-old practice of holding protests at Jantar Mantar and explore alternative locations with better facilities for peaceful demonstrators.
The petition also cited the Supreme Court’s 2018 judgment in Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan vs. Union of India, saying public-order concerns must be balanced against the right to peaceful assembly. The Centre’s response is awaited.
